page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the c4d family. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 126.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 7.88 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 10%. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier throughput. However, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations on large uncached blocks similarly align with middle-tier performance.

The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI, though it lacks AMX support. This hardware profile enables strong performance in specific tasks like text processing and small-model LLM text generation, which both rank in the top 10%. Conversely, database operations, static web serving, and medium-model LLM inference operate at average speeds. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier single-core compute capabilities, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications that do not scale linearly across massive core counts. It is suited for workloads such as memory-cached databases, text processing pipelines, lightweight LLM inference, and general-purpose applications requiring a substantial memory footprint without the overhead of high vCPU counts.

However, multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations remain in the average tier. The processor supports AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration but lacks AMX.
